summary: Mars Mission Architect is a browser-based game that turns spacecraft mission design into an experience anyone can understand. Players plan an Earth-to-Mars mission by choosing a launch window, a rocket, and science instruments within mass and budget limits. During the journey, random events such as solar storms and instrument failures test their decisions. At the end, a mission report reveals which choices increased risk the most. Built on real physics, including the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation, and on data from real Mars missions, the game shows that every engineering decision is a trade-off between mass, fuel, cost, and risk.
details: Mars Mission Architect is a browser-based educational game in which players design an Earth-to-Mars mission and learn how engineers balance conflicting constraints. The game has three stages. In the planning stage, players choose a launch window, a rocket, and scientific instruments while staying within mass and budget limits, with live indicators showing fuel, cost, risk, and science value. In the mission stage, the spacecraft travels to Mars and faces random events such as solar storms, instrument failures, or trajectory corrections, and the player must decide how to respond. In the final stage, a mission report summarizes the outcome and highlights which decisions increased risk the most. The game is grounded in real physics, using the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation to show how extra mass demands disproportionately more fuel, and it draws on real mission data from NASA and ESA missions such as Curiosity, Perseverance, and Mars Express. It is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, so it runs in any browser without installation. Our team combines data analysis, interface design, and animation skills, and we will start with a focused minimum viable version that can be expanded with more missions and destinations.
